national_raw_news.title: 5 hours ago | National 223 Har Ghar Tiranga campaign begins today, coinciding with 150th anniversary of India’s National Son...
national_raw_news.content: The Har Ghar Tiranga campaign will begin today and will run through 17th August. The initiative is aimed at encouraging citizens to hoist the National Flag and participate in activities celebrating patriotism, national unity and India’s cultural heritage. The campaign, which began in 2022 as part of the Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav celebrations, has since evolved into one of the country’s largest public participation movements. Over the years, it has emerged a true people’s movement that inspires citizens across regions and communities to celebrate the Tricolour as a symbol of India’s unity, honour and collective national identity. This year’s campaign holds special significance as it coincides with the 150th anniversary of India’s National Song, “Vande Mataram”, bringing together the National Flag and the National Song in a unique celebration of patriotism. As part of the celebrations, mass singing of Vande Mataram will be organised across the country. As part of the Independence Day commemorations, the Government will also observe Partition Horrors Remembrance Day on August 14 across the country to remember the suffering and displacement caused by the Partition of India. The observance will include silent marches, exhibitions on Partition, documentary screenings and other commemorative programmes across States and Union Territories. Inviting citizens to participate in the campaign, the Union Culture Ministry urged people to hoist the National Flag with pride, learn and sing Vande Mataram, take part in community activities and join the nation in remembering the sacrifices that shaped India’s journey to Independence. More than 200 Indian Embassies, High Commissions and Consulates will organise a series of events to mark the campaign. A key highlight this year will be the Surya Path Tiranga digital relay, in which 54 Indian Missions and Posts, selected according to the sunrise sequence across time zones, will participate. The relay will begin on 15th August from India’s easternmost diplomatic mission in Fiji and conclude at the Consulate General of India in San Francisco.

national_raw_news.title: 5 hours ago | National 150 Appointment of 30 Judges for High Courts of Madras, Calcutta, Madhya Pradesh and Karnataka notified
national_raw_news.content: The Centre has notified the appointment of 30 judges for High Courts of Madras, Calcutta, Madhya Pradesh, and Karnataka, with Madras High Court receiving the largest share of new appointees. According to a notification issued by the Ministry of Law and Justice, the appointments include 20 advocates and 10 judicial officers. Of the total, 15 judges have been appointed to the Madras High Court, 8 to the Calcutta High Court, 6 to the Karnataka High Court and one to the Madhya Pradesh High Court. The appointments were made by the President in consultation with the Chief Justice of India and the Supreme Court Collegium. The newly appointed judges are expected to take an oath and assume office in the coming days. The appointments are expected to help fill vacancies in the four High Courts and improve the disposal of pending cases.

national_raw_news.title: 5 hours ago | National 202 Amarnath Yatra to remain suspended from both Pahalgam and Baltal routes
national_raw_news.content: In Jammu and Kashmir, the annual Amarnath Yatra will remain suspended on both the Pahalgam and Baltal routes from today due to recent rains, repair work of pilgrimage tracks and the forecast of adverse weather conditions over the next few days. The decision to temporarily halt the yatra has been taken keeping in view the condition of the tracks as well as the weather forecast issued by the India Meteorological Department. No fresh Yatra convoy was allowed to leave the Bhagwati Nagar base camp in Jammu yesterday as a precautionary measure amid rains and inclement weather conditions prevailing in Ramban district and parts of Kashmir. Meanwhile, the 28th batch, comprising 1,202 pilgrims who had completed darshan at the Holy Cave and were staying at the Baltal base camp, was allowed to proceed towards Jammu in a convoy of 44 vehicles. The returning pilgrims included 867 males, 251 females, one child, 79 sadhus and four sadhvis. The convoy comprised 28 heavy vehicles, one medium motor vehicle, 11 light motor vehicles and four trucks. 3336 pilgrims performed darshan at the Holy Cave yesterday. The pilgrims included 2384 males, 569 females, 21 children, 20 sadhus, six sadhvis, four transgender pilgrims and 332 security personnel. With this, the total number of pilgrims who have performed darshan during the 2026 Yatra has reached 4 lakh 80 thousand and 19. The 57-day-long Amarnath Yatra commenced on July 3 simultaneously from both the traditional Chandanwari route in Anantnag district and the Baltal route in Ganderbal district and is scheduled to culminate with the traditional Chadi Mubarak ceremony on August 28. However, due to the recent rains, a necessity for the repair and maintenance of the Yatra tracks at vulnerable stretches has been felt, which is being undertaken by the Border Roads Organisation (BRO). The IMD has predicted adverse weather conditions over the next few days. Hence, the Yatra shall remain suspended from both routes with effect from today. Authorities have appealed to pilgrims to follow advisories issued by the competent authorities from time to time in the interest of their safety and the smooth conduct of the pilgrimage.

national_raw_news.title: 5 hours ago | Sports 94 Sagnik-Sayantan win Gold medal in Under-31 Pairs at 9th World Bridge Federation Youth Transnation...
national_raw_news.content: Sagnik Roy and Sayantan Kushari won the gold medal in the Under-31 Pairs at the 9th World Youth Transnational Championships in Hefei, China, yesterday. In the first elimination round, 34 pairs competed and the top 14 advanced to Flight A, including the Indian duo. They then competed in a round-robin format, with Sagnik and Sayantan finishing on top with 377.67 match points. M Fereneca and F Katusich of Croatia finished second with 357.78 match points, while China’s J Han and Z Wang took the third spot with 335.92 match points.

national_raw_news.title: NBA disburses over 3 crore rupees under Access and Benefit Sharing mechanism to 33 States/UTs and National Institutes
national_raw_news.content: The National Biodiversity Authority (NBA) has disbursed over 3 crore rupees as Access and Benefit Sharing (ABS) to 33 State Biodiversity Boards, Union Territory Biodiversity Councils and National Institutes. The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change said that the release covers a diverse range of India’s agrobiodiversity, including tomato, chilli, brinjal and deep-frozen Sahiwal cattle semen. It informed that cumulative ABS disbursements by the NBA have now exceeded 166 crore rupees. The Ministry also said that each release further strengthens the link between biodiversity conservation, scientific research and the livelihoods of the communities that conserve India’s rich biological resources.

national_raw_news.title: NIA arrests another accused in connection with seizure of huge consignment of illegal explosives in Malappuram
national_raw_news.content: The National Investigation Agency (NIA) has arrested another accused in connection with the seizure of a huge consignment of illegal explosives in Malappuram, Keralam. The Agency informed that the accused was arrested yesterday from Manjeri in the Malappuram district. NIA said that the accused is a main conspirator and was involved in the illegal procurement of the explosives seized in the case. The latest arrest comes a day after the NIA arrested three more accused from Vijayapura in Karnataka on Friday, taking the total number of arrests in the case to ten. The case relates to the seizure of 89,600 explosive sticks and 10,500 shock tubes from a lorry parked in the compound of Farha Hollow Bricks Company on the Chemmad-Thalappara Road in Malappuram. NIA further said that investigation into the larger conspiracy and the illegal procurement and movement of the explosives is continuing.

national_raw_news.title: Vice President CP Radhakrishnan pays tribute to freedom fighters of Quit India Movement
national_raw_news.content: Vice President CP Radhakrishnan has paid tributes to the freedom fighters who participated in the Quit India Movement. In a social media post, he said that they united the nation in the struggle for freedom, taking inspiration from Mahatma Gandhi’s clarion call of Do or Die. The Vice President added that their courage, sacrifice and patriotism continue to inspire generations.

national_raw_news.title: Pentagon orders US defense companies to accelerate weapons production and deliveries
national_raw_news.content: The Pentagon has ordered US defense companies to accelerate weapons production and deliveries as the Iran war has depleted key US munitions stockpiles. The Washington Post reported that Deputy Defense Secretary Steve Feinberg told defense industry leaders in a memo that they have 21 days to submit plans to drive significantly faster, more aggressive delivery schedules and increased production for critical capabilities. The Pentagon has also pursued framework agreements with major defense contractors and technology firms to expand production. But those agreements are nonbinding and depend on congressional funding. The directive comes as the Pentagon seeks to replenish stocks of weapons, including Patriot and Terminal High Altitude Area Defense (THAAD) interceptors. The Center for Strategic and International Studies said the global inventory of Patriot missiles had fallen from about 2,200 before the war to fewer than 827, while THAAD stocks dropped from 452 to less than 278. The Pentagon’s push comes as a 1.15 trillion US Dollar defense spending bill remains stalled in Congress, potentially delaying efforts to rapidly expand weapons production.

national_raw_news.title: China: Over 1,300 flights cancelled in Shanghai in view of Typhoon Dolphin
national_raw_news.content: In China, Shanghai’s two airports cancelled more than 1,300 flights and authorities relocated over 3 lakh people in surrounding regions as the country prepared for Typhoon Dolphin. The outer bands of the storm hit northern Taiwan yesterday, including the capital Taipei, bringing rain. Some Taiwanese airlines also cancelled their flights to China. The storm’s maximum sustained winds were estimated at about 162 kilometres per hour as of today morning. It is bringing heavy rains, creating a risk of severe flooding as well as landslides and is expected to hit Zhejiang province and northern parts of neighbouring Fujian province. Authorities are warning of severe landslide risks in Zhejiang. Shanghai’s Hongqiao and Pudong airports also cancelled about 60 per cent of expected flights. Authorities in Zhejiang evacuated some 3 lakh 90 thousand people in the city of Taizhou yesterday.

national_raw_news.title: US criticises China’s move at Scarborough Reef
national_raw_news.content: The United States has rejected China’s move to establish what it called a national nature reserve at Scarborough Reef, saying the measure could restrict Filipino fishermen’s access to their traditional fishing grounds, as reflected in the 2016 Arbitral Award. In a press release, the US State Department said this is yet another unilateral attempt by China to use dubious environmental and legal pretexts, backed by coercion, to advance its sweeping territorial and maritime claims in the South China Sea at the expense of its neighbours. The United States stands with its Ally, the Philippines, in support of a free and open Indo-Pacific, the statement further said. The statement followed China’s announcement of new management measures for the disputed feature, referred to by the Philippines and international legal documents as Scarborough Shoal. According to China Daily, the measures were issued on August 1 and consist of 16 articles aimed at managing the newly established national nature reserve. The measures establish a coordination mechanism among the four agencies to address major issues, strengthen cooperation and information-sharing, and enhance supervision and law enforcement against activities deemed illegal. The 2016 South China Sea Arbitral Award, issued by the arbitral tribunal constituted under the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS), found that there was no legal basis for China to claim historic rights to resources within the maritime areas falling within the Philippines’ exclusive economic zone. However, China has rejected the same.

national_raw_news.title: India’s medal tally rises to 3 at World Athletics Under-20 Championships 25 mins ago 18
national_raw_news.content: India’s medal tally rises to three at the World Athletics Under-20 Championships in the United States. India’s Basant Kumar Meghwal wins a silver in the high jump, while Shahnavaz Khan wins a bronze in the long jump today. In the men’s high jump, 19-year-old Meghwal cleared his personal best of 2.21 metres to win a silver medal. He became the first Indian to win a medal in the high jump at the World U-20 Championships. Algeria’s Younes Ayachi won the gold, while Great Britain’s Otis Poole took the bronze. In the men’s long jump, Shahnavaz clinched bronze with a best effort of 7.84 metres. The 18-year-old produced his best jump in his third attempt. Italy’s Daniele Inzoli won the gold medal with a jump of 7.97 metres, while Australia’s Mason McGroder took silver with a personal best of 7.96 metres. Earlier, in the javelin throw, Ashish Yadav won silver and became the second Indian after Neeraj Chopra to win at the World Athletics U20 Championships. Yadav produced his best throw of 74.09 metres in the third round yesterday.

national_raw_news.title: Ashmita Chaliha wins Korea Masters women’s singles title 2026 3 hours ago 146
national_raw_news.content: Indian shuttler Ashmita Chaliha produced a superb comeback to win the Korea Masters 2026, beating China’s Han Qian Xi in the women’s singles final this morning. The Assam shuttler recovered from losing the opening game to prevail 14-21, 21-14, and 21-14 in 53 minutes and claim her first BWF title. Earlier, Ashmita reached the final after defeating fellow Indian Rakshitha Ramraj 21-13, 16-21, 21-13 in the semifinal yesterday. While Han outplayed South Korea’s G Kim 22-20, 18-21, and 21-14 in the other semifinal to advance to the final. Ashmita Chaliha had won the gold medal at the 2024 Asia Team Championships. At the 2019 South Asian Games, she had secured gold medals in both the women’s singles and team events.
